conviction_note: A no-release, no-call 10-Q on a stock that is now a fixed-price cash stub four weeks from closing has almost no room to move (20d realised vol 32.6% = ~2%/day, tape flat +0.39% over 20d); I net a modestly asymmetric upside from the realistic chance the Q1 going-concern 'substantial doubt' language is alleviated in tonight's text against a smaller downside from the 7/31 cash balance sitting closer to the undisclosed-in-any-press-release $25m Minimum Cash Amount, and land near +1%.

findings.finding: Tonight's 10-Q is the first Domo filing issued after the deal was signed (7/22), HSR early-terminated (8/25) and the close pulled forward to end-September with no financing condition - which under ASC 205-40 gives management a strong basis to remove the 'substantial doubt exists about the Company's ability to continue as a going concern' language carried in the Q1 10-Q, a machine-readable flag change arriving with no press release or call to dilute it.
findings.why_not_priced: There is no sell-side preview, no earnings release and no call for this event, so nothing has framed what the filing text will say; if the market were positioning for a going-concern removal on a stub trading 21% below the company's own stated $4.84 closing net cash, the tape would not be flat (+0.93% over 5 sessions, +0.39% over 20) through an 8/31 release that disclosed early HSR termination, 'no financing condition' and a 'debt-free balance sheet'. Going-concern flag changes are picked up by screeners and automated news precisely because they are a binary field, and on an 875k-share/day $170m-cap name that flag is the credit-risk component the equity is discounting.
findings.independence: The 8/31 company release independently establishes the facts that make alleviation defensible - early HSR termination 8/25, close expected end of September, no financing condition, debt-free post-close: https://www.stocktitan.net/news/DOMO/domo-announces-timing-for-second-quarter-fiscal-2027-financial-kku4cu17uwdk.html (2026-08-31 18:00 ET). Note this finding and the next one both read the same Q1 10-Q, so the Q1 10-Q should be collapsed to one source cluster.

findings.finding: Domo paid ~$5.9m of cash lender and legal fees on effectiveness of the June 12 forbearance - i.e. inside the quarter being reported tonight - against cash of $39.1m at 4/30, while the purchase price is '$400m minus the amount, if any, by which $25 million (the Minimum Cash Amount) exceeds our estimation' of cash, with 'no upward adjustment' for cash above $25m; so the 7/31 cash line lands in a narrow corridor where a shortfall cuts proceeds dollar-for-dollar and an excess is transferred to Progress for free.
findings.why_not_priced: The $25m Minimum Cash Amount and the no-upward-adjustment clause appear only in a Schedule 14C - a document with no vote to solicit, no proxy fight, no analyst summary and, judging by the completely flat tape since it was mailed on 8/24, no readership. The $4.84 headline from 7/22 is a single point estimate with no published sensitivity, and neither of Domo's two press releases mentions a minimum-cash construct at all; if the market had modelled it, the stub's discount would visibly widen or narrow with the cash trajectory rather than sitting still. The $5.9m cash fee is buried in the Q1 forbearance note and post-dates the 4/30 balance sheet, so it is absent from every screener's last-reported cash figure.
findings.independence: The $5.9m cash forbearance fee, the $39.1m cash balance and the $10m minimum-pledged-cash covenant come from a different document, the Q1 FY27 10-Q: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001505952/000162828026043173/domo10q-20260430.htm (2026-06-15). That 10-Q is shared with the finding above, so the two are not fully independent.

searched_and_found_nothing: Insider activity since the deal: no Form 4 and no 13D/G filed after 2026-08-14, so no insider or activist has bought the 21% discount to stated net cash - a tell that would have mattered, and its absence is not a tradable finding
The two 13Gs filed 8/14 are Citadel Securities and Susquehanna/G1 market-making books as of 6/30/2026 (pre-deal), not event-driven accumulation
No 8-K has been filed since 2026-07-22 - the HSR early termination and the 8/31 timing release were not 8-K'd, so there is no quiet filing to mine
The Section 382 tax-benefits preservation plan (4.9% trigger, expires 2029-07-20, 8-A12B filed 7/22) is public and structurally caps any accumulator, but it is not new information for tonight

The DEFM14C's plain-English 'Will I receive any of the proceeds from the Transactions? No.' and 'The Company does not intend to liquidate following the Closing' are the reason the stub trades below net cash, but they have been mailed to holders since 8/24 with zero price response - absorbed or ignored, either way not an edge for one filing

Company-level tax on the asset-sale gain: the 14C's tax section covers stockholders only, and the FY26 10-K income-tax footnote would not render, so I could not establish the pre-2018 vs post-2017 NOL split that determines whether the 80%-of-taxable-income cap leaks cash tax against the $246m estimate - dropped for lack of a verifiable number
No quantified dollar figure for executive severance / RSU acceleration could be pulled out of the 14C's 'Interests of the Company's Directors and Officers' section
Progress Software has not spoken since 7/22 (FY26 Q3 ends 8/31, call is later in September), so there is no counterparty commentary post-dating Domo's last statement
No announced acquisition target, LOI or capital-return plan for the post-close shell anywhere in company sources
baseline_tension: There is no skew or implied move to agree or disagree with, and the run-up is effectively zero, so the tension is with the baseline's 18% median: my read is that a filing-only, no-call event on a signed fixed-price cash stub belongs an order of magnitude below that, and the two things I found roughly offset into a small positive rather than any 18%-scale move.
